You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in the `vub300` driver by reverting from device-managed allocation (`devm_mmc_alloc_host`) to manual allocation (`mmc_alloc_host`). This ensures the `mmc_host` (and the embedded `vub300_mmc_host`) is freed only when the driver’s explicit reference count drops to zero, preventing premature freeing when the driver is unbound without a physical disconnect.

### Modifications in **drivers/mmc/host/vub300.c**
- **`vub300_delete()`** (kref callback):  
  Added `mmc_free_host(mmc)` before the comment noting that the free also deallocates the `vub300` structure. This ensures the `mmc_host` is properly released when the last reference is dropped.

- **`vub300_probe()`**:  
  - Changed `devm_mmc_alloc_host(&udev->dev, ...)` to `mmc_alloc_host(sizeof(*vub300), &udev->dev)`.  
  - Replaced the `error4` label with a new `err_free_host` label that calls `mmc_free_host(mmc)`.  
  - Modified several error paths (after USB control message failures) to jump to `err_free_host` instead of `error4`.  
  - The existing `error6` label (which deletes a timer) now falls through into `err_free_host`, ensuring the host is freed in that error path as well.

### Relationships
- The switch from device-managed to manual allocation decouples the `mmc_host` lifetime from the USB device’s devres group, avoiding use-after-free when the driver unbinds (e.g., on probe deferral) before the physical device is disconnected.
- All code paths that allocate the host must free it on failure; the new `err_free_host` label provides a single point for that cleanup.
- The `vub300_delete()` function is the final release point, so adding `mmc_free_host()` there completes the manual lifetime management. Together, these changes ensure the host memory is freed exactly when the last reference is released, preventing both use-after-free and memory leaks.
